proposal.summary: DVC (treeverse/dvc 3.67.1) keeps its win on the narrow claim it actually earns — versioned snapshot/restore — and the evidence for that claim got stronger, not weaker, since the 2026-09-22 gates file was written. The repo's own gap-wave-2 work (2026-09-23, evidence_class native_proven -> local_integration, 5 rounds of Codex+independent-Opus adversarial fixing) ran a real 4-way store comparison (baseline hash-manifest, DVC, PyIceberg 0.12.0, ArcticDB v6.26.0) on a materialized fixture: DVC and the baseline are the only arms that keep exact per-file sha256 (Iceberg/ArcticDB rewrite source files into their own formats, "not_supported by design"); under two concurrent writers, baseline/DVC/Iceberg lost 0 rows every time, but ArcticDB silently lost 50-150 of every 100-300 rows across repeated rounds -- confirming, by measurement rather than by license text alone, its own installed docstring's "concurrent writers to a single symbol are not supported" limitation. That, plus BSL-1.1 (source-available, forbids resale as a hosted "Database Service") and ~18x DVC's storage footprint on the same fixture, is a decisive strike against the researcher's ArcticDB pick. Iceberg is a genuine, verified trade-off (native time-travel, auto-retry concurrency safety, faster reads) but not a proven win -- it fails the byte-identical-snapshot bar the layer's requirement names, and needs an added catalog service; it stays "conditional," not promoted. Two of the layer's own seven listed open gaps are already closed by evidence layers.json/the 2026-09-22 adjudication have not caught up to: gap 4 ("no executed comparison measures... across the candidate stores") is settled by the comparison above, and gap 5/6 ("OpenLineage event persistence... and MLflow run-to-dataset bindings, remain unqualified") is settled by a 2026-09-23 local_integration run where openlineage-python 1.53.0 persisted schema-valid, tamper-detecting lineage events and mlflow 3.16.1 bound them to logged datasets -- directly contradicting both the researcher's own "UNEXECUTED"/"no receipt... wired" framing and the 2026-09-22 A/B adjudication that excluded OpenLineage from the winner set on exactly that (now outdated) basis. I therefore recommend adding OpenLineage+MLflow as a qualified lineage-persistence pairing (not displacing DVC, which was never meant to do this job). Separately, the catalog's own critic already flags foundation-socraticode as mis-tagged into this layer (it is a code-retrieval index, not a security-identity/provenance tool) -- a clean "demote, don't keep by default" finding I second. What remains a genuine, unclosed open_gap is the compound identity/corporate-action/licensing half of the requirement: the 235 ticker-collision and pre-2020-delisting gates are still not_established, and the repository's own 2026-09-23/09-26 sweeps already found and refuted every free OSS candidate they tried (BlackFalconData delisted-stocks-list, fja05680/sp500, stale Nasdaq Data Link). I independently WebFetched OpenFIGI's own API docs today and confirmed it is current-state mapping only (figi/ticker/name/exchCode/securityType fields; no listing/delisting date, no ticker-history, no active/inactive flag) -- it cannot resolve the 235 collisions, which need historical validity windows, not a permanent identifier. PermID's only Python client is 5.5 years stale and its coverage of this specific need is unverified, not confirmed. The only recorded viable closers (Databento, Sharadar -- explicitly not yet individually refuted by the 2026-09-23 sweep, QuantConnect Security Master/AlgoSeek, QuantRocket usstock) are all paid and explicitly gated as a user-decision, outside this read-only task's scope.

winner_status.note: Restore claim is now native_proven with real rigor: an initial literal test failure (2 git-tracked .gitignore files not restored by `dvc checkout` alone) was caught and fixed in fix-round-3 (git checkout for git-tracked files + dvc checkout for DVC-tracked files restores the full 16-file tree; a 1-byte tamper is caught by diff/dvc status and repaired by `dvc checkout --force`). The 2026-09-23 four-store comparison additionally shows DVC tied for best on lineage-native-field count (4/6, tied with Iceberg) and zero-loss concurrency (tied with baseline and Iceberg), and uniquely (with baseline) preserving exact per-file sha256, which Iceberg/ArcticDB structurally cannot. DVC is markedly slower (368-504ms vs Iceberg's 17-149ms) but that figure includes CLI subprocess overhead per the receipt's own limits, not an apples-to-apples in-process comparison. None of this closes the layer's separate identity/corporate-action/licensing obligations, which DVC was never positioned to address.

Tagged as a co-default in this layer by the broader catalog (catalogs/sota-convergence/manifest-20260923.json, sota-convergence/README.md table row 'Identity & provenance | dvc 3.67.1 . socraticode 1.14.0'), but NOT listed among this layer's winners in layers.json, and the project's own critic already recorded 'review_status: demotion_proposed' with the exact reasoning I'd give: 'SocratiCode is a code-retrieval index, not a security-identity or provenance tool, so no native_proven default addresses the layer's purpose. It stays default in the foundation code-retrieval layer.' No evidence anywhere ties it to data identity, provenance or corporate-action semantics. Recommend it be dropped from this layer's roster entirely (keep it only under agents-models-workers/foundation code-retrieval, where it already is a winner).

challengers.name: OpenLineage (openlineage-python)
challengers.why_better: Was excluded from this layer's winner set by the 2026-09-22 A/B adjudication specifically because its native_workflow was 'Prospective and UNEXECUTED' and 'only builds a Dataset object... no transport or network emission' (adjudication file + catalogs/us-equities/data-research.json lines 819-859). One day later the repo's own gap-wave-2 run reverses that characterization: openlineage-python 1.53.0's FileTransport actually persisted START/COMPLETE RunEvents for a real materialize+select run, with a custom dataset-version facet equal to the manifest's snapshot_sha256/per-file sha256 and knowledge-cutoff/horizon facets consistent across events; a fresh process read them back with 0 problems, all 4 events validated against the official OpenLineage 2-0-2 core RunEvent schema, and all 5 planted-defect detector controls (tampered facet, removed output, removed input, renamed output, malformed schema) were correctly flagged -- after 4 adversarial fix rounds (2x Codex, 1x independent Opus, 1x Codex again) that caught and corrected real measurement bugs along the way. This directly closes the exact text of the layer's own listed gap ('OpenLineage event persistence and consistent version/cutoff facets... remain unqualified'), which layers.json has not yet been updated to reflect.
challengers.evidence_level: native_execution (repo's own 'local_integration' tier: package actually installed under uv and run in a network-isolated venv against a real fixture, not merely read; scope is a synthetic 2-run fixture, not production acquisition data)
challengers.trial_plan: Already run: bash blueprints/gap-wave2-20260923/us-equities__identity-provenance/run_lineage_mlflow.sh (pin openlineage-python==1.53.0); output evidence/artifacts/gap-wave2-20260923/us-equities__identity-provenance/5-openlineage-mlflow-bindings.json, outcome settled. Next bounded step to promote from 'conditional' to an adopted lineage role: point the same emit+readback pair at the real Alpaca/EdgarTools acquisition adapters (blueprints/us-equities/authenticated-data, blueprints/us-equities/catalyst-provenance) instead of the synthetic nanosecond-replay fixture. Pass criterion: a fresh-process readback reproduces every event/facet with 0 problems (as already shown) AND the event's version facet equals the real acquisition receipt's own recorded snapshot hash bit-for-bit. Overturn condition: if the live acquisition adapters have no stable hashable snapshot to bind to, or if cross-run querying later requires a real lineage backend rather than a local ndjson file -- note the obvious backend, Marquez, was independently re-examined in this same 2026-09-23 sweep and refuted (formal releases stalled at 0.50.0 since 2024-10-24; its cited endorsement quote was not found on the fetched page), so it should get its own bounded trial before being assumed as the default persistence layer.

challengers.name: MLflow
challengers.why_better: The researcher's own packet said 'no receipt in the repository shows it wired to an actual dataset yet.' The repo's 2026-09-23 gap-wave-2 run refutes that as of today: mlflow 3.16.1 on a local SQLite tracking store logged both a materialize run and a select run via mlflow.log_input, and the bindings (names, digests, sources, plus custom file_sha256/snapshot_sha256/openlineage.run_id tags) were read back through MlflowClient/get_run and matched the manifest exactly, in a fresh process. This closes the exact text of the layer's own listed gap ('...MLflow run-to-dataset bindings, remain unqualified'). One real, useful finding surfaced along the way: MLflow's dataset 'digest' field is capped at 36 characters, so this project's 64-char sha256 cannot be the digest itself and must instead ride in a dataset-input tag -- a concrete integration detail any future adopter needs, not a cosmetic note.
challengers.evidence_level: native_execution (repo's own 'local_integration' tier: package actually installed and run against a real fixture with two logged runs; scope is one materialize run + one select run on synthetic data, not a production experiment corpus)
challengers.trial_plan: Already run: same run_lineage_mlflow.sh invocation (pin mlflow==3.16.1), output in the same 5-openlineage-mlflow-bindings.json receipt (C5.3/C5.4 criteria, outcome settled). Next bounded step: bind a real skfolio/EdgarTools research run (this layer's neighboring research-factors-ml winners) to its consumed dataset via the same log_input pattern, and confirm the OpenLineage run-id tag written by this layer's adapter matches the emitted OpenLineage event for the same acquisition. Pass criterion: MlflowClient.get_run().inputs.dataset_inputs for a real research run reads back the same acquisition-receipt hash used elsewhere in the pipeline. Overturn condition: if a real multi-dataset research run needs more than the 36-character digest MLflow supports natively (already known to require the tag workaround), or if MLflow's own dataset-lineage UI/query surface proves unnecessary overhead versus just reading the OpenLineage ndjson file directly for this project's bounded scale.

rejected.name: ArcticDB (man-group/ArcticDB)
rejected.reason: refuted: the 2026-09-23 four-store comparison measured ArcticDB silently losing appends its own writers reported as successful under two concurrent writers to one symbol -- 50/100 rows at n=10 and 130-150/300 at n=30, repeatably across multiple rounds -- matching its own installed docstring's documented limitation ('concurrent writers to a single symbol are not supported'). Compounded by license (Business Source License 1.1: source-available, not OSI-approved, forbids resale as a hosted 'Database Service', converts to Apache-2.0 only 2 years after each release) and ~18x DVC's storage footprint on the identical fixture (225,536 vs 10,887 bytes).

rejected.name: OpenFIGI
rejected.reason: off-requirement, verified today: WebFetched the official API documentation directly -- the mapping response is current-state only (figi, ticker, name, exchCode, securityType, compositeFIGI, etc.); no listing/delisting date, ticker-change-history or active/inactive status field exists in any documented endpoint. It cannot resolve the layer's 235 dated ticker collisions, which need historical validity windows, not a permanent-but-timeless identifier. (FIGI's own permanence guarantee -- 'once issued... will not change' -- describes identifier stability, not historical security coverage.)

researched_candidates.name: DVC (treeverse/dvc)
researched_candidates.fit: Current catalog winner for this layer; pin matches upstream exactly. The only material change since the pin is organizational (Iterative.ai -> lakeFS stewardship), not technical -- confirmed the repository URL treeverse/dvc is correct and current, not a catalog error: iterative/dvc now resolves to it. DVC's file/artifact model has no native concept of security identity, corporate actions, or licensed-data eligibility; it only versions whatever files are handed to it, so it stays a partial answer to the layer's requirement even where it is the right tool.

researched_candidates.name: Apache Iceberg / PyIceberg
researched_candidates.fit: The strongest already-catalogued challenger to DVC's file-based snapshot model for a tabular equity dataset, because time-travel is a native table-catalog feature. The existing 2026-09-23 sweep already probed this territory via Nessie and Delta Lake (both refuted as redundant with Iceberg on this non-Spark stack); PyIceberg itself has never been run against this project's own fixture, so it stays source_review only, not a demonstrated win.

researched_candidates.name: ArcticDB
researched_candidates.fit: Directly relevant to the layer's 'version/cutoff facets' gap for equity bars, and a plausible table-native alternative to DVC. Important correction to carry forward: this project's LICENSE.txt is Business Source License 1.1 -- it forbids offering ArcticDB as a hosted 'Database Service' to third parties and only converts to a permissive license two years after each version's release. GitHub's own license.spdx_id field reports 'NOASSERTION', which understates this; the existing catalog record for ArcticDB does not mention BSL either. Any adoption decision needs to weigh that restriction explicitly.

researched_candidates.name: Lance (pylance / lance-format)
researched_candidates.fit: The best fit in this whole set for the layer's explicit 'version/cutoff facets' gap language, because versioning is native to the file format rather than a side-car tool layered on top of Parquet, and it drops directly under the stack's existing DuckDB/Parquet path. It versions bytes, not securities, so it still needs this project's own identity/corporate-action logic on top, exactly as DVC does today.

researched_candidates.name: Delta Sharing
researched_candidates.fit: Solves a different sub-problem than DVC: cross-organization distribution of a licensed, versioned dataset with enforced access control, not intra-project snapshot/restore. Useful only if this project needs to hand off or receive an equity dataset under access control; it does not itself establish security identity or corporate-action completeness. Distinct from delta-io/delta (the Spark table format the existing sweep already refuted as redundant with Iceberg) -- Delta Sharing is a sharing protocol, not a competing table format, so that refutation does not carry over.

researched_candidates.name: OpenLineage
researched_candidates.fit: A wire format/emitter, not a store -- it defines events but does not itself answer 'what fed this snapshot.' Confirmed active today (pushed 2026-09-26), pin unchanged and current. Needs pairing with a persistence layer (Marquez, or a project-local sink) to actually close the layer's lineage-reconstruction gap #6; alone it produces events and closes none of the requirement by itself.

researched_candidates.name: Marquez
researched_candidates.fit: The leading open persistence store for OpenLineage events and the most direct existing-OSS answer to gap #6, but its formal release cadence has stalled almost 2 years (0.50.0, 2024-10-24) despite continued commits (pushed 2026-09-15) -- reconfirmed today unchanged from the 2026-09-23 sweep. Already source-reviewed and adversarially checked there; the concrete overturn test (emit real events from this project's own ingestion adapters for one acquisition day, then query them back) remains unexecuted.

researched_candidates.name: MLflow
researched_candidates.fit: Strong for binding a research run to the dataset version it consumed, helping 'reproducible analytical snapshots,' but it is an ML-experiment tracker, not a source-identity or corporate-action tool -- it does not acquire, license-check, or validate equity data itself. Already a catalog conditional; no receipt in the repository shows it wired to an actual dataset yet.

researched_candidates.name: Great Expectations
researched_candidates.fit: The strongest known direct competitor to the catalog's Pandera pick for this layer's 'reject data whose eligibility is unknown' clause, because it persists a queryable rejection/audit record rather than raising an in-process exception. Already source-reviewed and adversarially checked in the 2026-09-23 sweep (survives=false only for lack of a head-to-head trial against Pandera, and because its connector list omits DuckDB/Polars, which Pandera already supports); I reconfirm the org transfer and that gap are both still current.

researched_candidates.name: OpenFIGI
researched_candidates.fit: Best primary-source fit for the layer's 'permanent security identity' half of the requirement, which the current winner (DVC) does not address at all. Free, open, run by Bloomberg under a public-standards body, and not a GitHub-shaped project -- exactly the kind of find the task's 'beyond stars and awesome lists' instruction is asking for. Whether its coverage actually includes listing/delisting dates that resolve the specific 235 collisions is unverified; only running that check would move this past source_review. No official GitHub client SDK exists (only third-party wrappers such as talsan/openfigi and jwergieluk/openfigi were found).

researched_candidates.name: PermID (LSEG Open PermID)
researched_candidates.fit: Directly on point for identity and a genuine independent second source to cross-check against OpenFIGI -- the kind of convergence check this layer's requirement wants. Flagged unmaintained at the package level: the official OpenPermID Python client on PyPI has not shipped since 2021-03-05 (5.5 years), even though LSEG's hosted developer portal for the underlying API reads as current in 2026; using it today would mean calling the REST API directly rather than relying on that stale client package.

researched_candidates.name: backtest-bias (Finance-broski)
researched_candidates.fit: Directly on point for the requirement's survivorship/eligibility-rejection clause and the layer's own open pre-2020-delisting gate. researched_candidates.fit: Directly names 'corporate-action factor chains' and point-in-time back-adjustment -- exactly the requirement's 'preserve... corporate actions' clause and squarely inside this layer's open gaps. But it, falsification-ledger, and ashare-data-immunity were all created by the same holdout-labs account on the same day (2026-08-18) with 0-1 stars each and no independent adopters found in this check -- treat as one person's tool portfolio, not independently validated OSS, until an outside adopter is shown. I only checked GitHub metadata, not the adjustment code itself.

researched_candidates.name: Shingou signal log (shingou-io/shingou-signal-log)
researched_candidates.fit: The clearest working instance in this candidate set of the layer's own language: 'immutable capture and cutoff rejection.' It is crypto-news-specific and tiny (0 stars, no license), but the mechanism -- commit a hash of each point-in-time bucket to a public append-only log at publish time, verify later that nothing was rewritten -- is a genuinely different, more concrete pattern than DVC's git-style file versioning, and directly transferable to equity bars or corporate-action revisions. The awesome-list input actually cited the wrong repo (shingou-io/shingou-integrations, which is only exchange-bot plugin glue); the real hash-chain verifier lives at shingou-io/shingou-signal-log and, notably, ships with no LICENSE file, which anyone reusing the pattern should flag before copying code.

researched_candidates.name: OpenPM: Auditable Point-in-Time Evaluation for LLM Portfolio-Management Agents
researched_candidates.fit: The strongest 2026-dated, genuinely 'beyond stars and awesome lists' find for this layer: a methodology, not an installable component, but the closest primary source to a worked reference implementation of the requirement's central clause (reject data unavailable at decision time; produce an auditable, reproducible record). No code repository was found in the fetched content, so it cannot be adopted as a dependency today; it is evidence for how to design this project's own point-in-time gate and audit-artifact schema, not a library to install. Submitted 2026-08-06 (arXiv id 2608.09988), 10 authors with a visible Rutgers (Metaxas) affiliation.
